To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed an atomic convolutional neural networks that can predict protein-ligand binding affinity directly from atomic coordinates of the complex, and that the model is competitive with state-of-the art cheminformatics based methods.

we developed an end-to-end differentiable deep learning model for protein-ligand interaction prediction and that the model outperforms state-of-the-art machine learning and cheminformatics based methods.
we developed a novel deep learning architecture for predicting protein-ligand binding affinity that is able to identify and quantify non-covalent interactions in protein-ligand crystal structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new deep learning architectures that allow for the prediction of protein-ligands binding affinity.
the development of deep neural networks for predicting the binding affinity of a ligand to a given protein target.
the development of new machine learning methods for the prediction of protein-ligands binding affinity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art in terms of mean absolute error (0.72 kcal/mol) and mean absolute percentage error (24.5%) on the PDBbind v2015 dataset, and that it achieves a comparable performance to state-of-the-art approaches in terms of correlation coefficient and root mean square error.
our model is able to learn non-trivial chemical interactions and predict binding free energy of protein-ligands complexes from the atomic coordinates.
this work represents the state-of-the-art in structure-based bioactive prediction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an end-to-end, fully differentiable, deep learning-based method for predicting the binding free energies between a protein and a ligand from their 3D coordinates.
we developed a general 3D spatial convolution operation for molecular modeling, which we applied to structure-based bio-activity prediction.
we are able to learn the interaction strength of non-covalent interactions from atomic coordinates and predict the binding free energy for protein-ligand systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
atomic convolutional neural networks offer an exciting new paradigm for structure-based bioactivity modeling and prediction.
the atomic convolution operation can be used for predicting non-covalent interactions in protein-ligand binding complexes.

atomic-level convolutional neural networks can learn the non-trivial physics of protein-ligands binding from data and that they can be used to predict the binding free energy with a high degree of accuracy.
